title: Sketch y=|3x-5| and y=x+2, and solve |3x-5|=x+2

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF (modulus bars checked on the rendered page). Steps and marks from the official MS PDF. Both (a) and (b) are kept: the sketch and the equation (no inequality). Fully manual, steps only, because (a) is a sketch and (b) has two official roots in one part.

stem:
(a) Sketch, on the same diagram, the graphs of \(y=\lvert 3x-5\rvert\) and \(y=x+2\).

(b) Solve the equation \(\lvert 3x-5\rvert=x+2\).

steps.name: vshape
steps.text_tex: (a) Draw a V-shaped graph with its vertex on the positive x-axis.
steps.note: MS: B1 Draw V-shaped graph with vertex on positive x-axis.

steps.name: line
steps.text_tex: (a) Draw a correct graph of y = x+2 with a smaller positive gradient, crossing the y-axis between 0 and the y-intercept of the V-shaped graph.
steps.note: MS: B1 Draw correct graph of y=x+2 with smaller positive gradient. Crossing y-axis between 0 and y-intercept of first graph.

steps.name: same
steps.note: MS: B1 Solve 3x-5 = x+2 to obtain x=7/2.

steps.name: opp
steps.text_tex: (b) Attempt the solution of a linear equation in which the signs of 3x and x are different.
steps.note: MS: M1 Attempt solution of linear equation where signs of 3x and x are different.

steps.name: ans
steps.text_tex: (b) Obtain x = 3/4. (The two roots are 7/2 and 3/4. Alternative: state or imply (3x-5)^2 = (x+2)^2, attempt the 3-term quadratic, and obtain both roots.)
steps.note: MS: A1 Obtain x=3/4. Alternative method: B1 non-modulus equation (3x-5)^2=(x+2)^2; M1 attempt 3-term quadratic; A1 obtain both roots.

title: Sketch y=|2x-9| and y=5x-3, and solve |2x-9|=5x-3

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF (modulus bars checked on the rendered page). Steps and marks from the official MS PDF. Both (a) and (b) are kept: the sketch and the equation (no inequality). Fully manual, steps only, because (a) is a sketch. The only valid root is 12/7; x=2 is not a solution.

stem:
(a) Sketch, on the same diagram, the graphs of \(y=\lvert 2x-9\rvert\) and \(y=5x-3\).

(b) Solve the equation \(\lvert 2x-9\rvert=5x-3\).

steps.name: vshape
steps.text_tex: (a) Draw a V-shaped graph with its vertex on the positive x-axis.
steps.note: MS: *B1 Draw V-shaped graph with vertex on positive x-axis.

steps.name: line
steps.text_tex: (a) Draw a more or less correct graph of y = 5x-3 with a greater gradient, crossing the x-axis between the origin and the vertex of the V-shaped graph.
steps.note: MS: DB1 Draw (more or less) correct graph of y=5x-3 with greater gradient, crossing x-axis between origin and vertex of first graph.

steps.name: opp
steps.text_tex: (b) Attempt the solution of a linear equation in which the signs of 2x and 5x are different.
steps.note: MS: M1 Attempt solution of linear equation where signs of 2x and 5x are different.

steps.name: ans
steps.text_tex: (b) Solve -2x+9 = 5x-3 to obtain 12/7, or 1.71 or better, and give no second answer. (Alternative: attempt the 3-term quadratic (2x-9)^2 = (5x-3)^2, which is 7x^2+2x-24=0, and obtain 12/7 with no second answer. The candidate x=2 does not satisfy the original equation.)
steps.note: MS: A1 and no second answer. Obtain 12/7, 1.71 or better. Alternative: M1 attempt 3-term quadratic to obtain at least one value of x; A1 obtain 12/7, 1.71 or better, and no second answer.
